newsitem.title: FINLAND: NCC sees modest '97 for European building.
newsitem.headline: NCC sees modest '97 for European building.

text.p: Swedish construction group NCC said on Thursday that 1997 will be a modest year for the European construction industry, but that prospects for next year were brighter.
"I think we can be more optimistic about 1998, but 1997 will be a modest year," NCC managing director Jan Sjoqvist told a seminar here.

Sjoqvist displayed graphs showing an industry forecast for zero growth in house building, less than one percent growth in non-residential building and a slight drop in civil engineering construction in the European Union in 1997.
He also forecast a 2.4 percent drop in total construction in Germany this year.
"Germany is by far the biggest market. Unfortunately it is that market that will perhaps be the weakest in the short term," Sjoqvist said.
"That will affect the whole European construction market," he added.
Sjoqvist said a forecast of 2.7 percent growth in construction in Sweden this year could be too optimistic.
"We don't quite believe in this... We think growth will be slightly less," Sjoqvist said, pointing to the strength of the Swedish crown as one factor likely to curb growth.
Asked how building industry profits would hold up if volume growth remained sluggish this year, Sjoqvist said:
"There is a strong connection between volumes and profits... That is the best indication of how profits will develop."
In November, NCC said its full-year 1996 earnings after financial items would be only slightly better than the 406 million crowns booked in January-September.
But Sjoqvist said 1998 looked brighter for construction in Sweden and Finland.
"Sweden and Finland are countries where recovery will come about in 1998," Sjoqvist said.
In the future, Nordic construction companies would need to form alliances with building groups in other countries to compete successfully on the European market, he said.
"We are too small to compete alone," he added.
